steps.text: In a large skillet combine the Worcestershire sauce and ground black pepper. Add the chicken and simmer over medium heat until the sauce begins to boil. Reduce heat to low and let simmer for 15 to 20 minutes. Turn chicken occasionally, spooning sauce over it. The sauce will thicken. Let cool and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: The Easiest Blackened Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Chicken breasts simmered in Worcestershire sauce and a hearty dose of ground black pepper for extra heat.
raw_recipe.name: The Easiest Blackened Chicken

review.reviewBody: After avoiding this recipe for months, believing that it couldn't be very good, I finally tried it and am beyond impressed with how it turned out. This is so simple and easy and the taste is wonderful. Watch the pepper, because it does get very spicy. Great to use this chicken with the refrigerated pasta and sauces for Blackened Chicken Alfredo. Family loves it!

First time I made this, it wasn't good at all. I tweaked it like this: 1 cup Worcestershire Sauce, 1 cup sliced whole mushrooms, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tbsp brown sugar, half a handful of fresh basil or you can use 1 tbsp dried, 1 pinch sea salt, 1 tsp olive oil, and 1 tbsp minced garlic... Boiled chicken thighs for 10 minutes. Sauteed minced garlic, sliced mushrooms, and basil in olive oil before adding other ingredients, cooked according to directions and served over a bed of fresh, shredded lettuce, and white rice to absorb the sauce. Very good, but we love garlic, so if it isn't your cup of tea, omit the garlic powder. Kids love it!

I only gave the recipe 3 stars since I had to make some modifications to it. The basic concept was good. I also took some of the others revisions & ran with them. Here was my version: 1/2 cup Worcestershire 1/2 cup Low Sodium Soy Sauce 1 tsp dry mustard 1 tbsp brown sugar 1 tsp black pepper 1 tsp lime juice I also browned the chicken pieces briefly before adding the liquid, brought it to a boil then reduced the heat. I will definitely make this again. It was a hit with even picky eaters of the house.

This recipe turned out delicious. Instead of using just black pepper I cut that to 1/2 tsp and added 1 tsp. of cajun seasoning called "Slap ya Mama" and 2 minced cloves of garlic. I then used the cooked chicken with penne noodles and alfredo cheese sauce topped with 1 cup. mozzarella cheese and dried basil. It was super delicious and will continue to cook my chicken this way for that dish from now on.

I really, really enjoyed this recipe, as does my fiance. It super quick, easy and tasty! I've made it twice now; once as is and once sauteing onions and garlic first. I prefer it with the onions and garlic. Note: Do Not be surprised if it tastes a lot like Worcestershire sauce. Worcestershire sauce is a strong flavor and is the dominant ingredient in this dish.

I added a little brown sugar, chopped garlic and onions per some of the reviews. I halved the amount of pepper because it sounded kind of excessive. 
The chicken was moist and flavorful and I enjoyed it. Funnily enough my boyfriend (who is not a picky eater at all) did not like it. I have no idea why not. 
I didn't have any rice so I served it with mashed potatoes.

Nice spicy taste, but a little too much. We added onions and served with white rice. Really liked adding some blue cheese dressing on the side for dippig. (cooling) Next time I would cut the pepper to 1t and may cut the worchestershire down a little.

This recipe is super easy & my family loves it! Its my go to recipe when I'm not in the mood to cook. In less then two minutes the chicken is bubbling away and I can move on to something else. I've tried both chicken breasts & chicken thighs and I think thighs are best because they come out nice and moist.
I don't know if this counts, but I made this w/Dale's steak sauce b/c I didn't have Worcestershire & it was really good-super quick & easy.
Yum! I used 3 chicken breasts (cut into 1-inch cubes) and 1/2 cup of Worcestshire sauce. I added fresh mushrooms and had this on angel hair pasta with Alfredo sauce. Sooooooo good!!!

Wonderful! I sliced some onion and added to the Worcestershire sauce. I also sprinkled chicken breast with Emeril's Essence seasoning before adding to the sauce. I will surely serve this to guests. Delicious!

I've made good blackened chicken with recipes from this site. Why I didn't choose one of those I can only guess is speed in getting it in the pan, but combining spices isn't that timeconsuming. Cook time is very close. It wasn't until I tasted it did I realize that I essentially making plump "chicken jerky." 'Hoping this can be saved by using in Brunswick stew. No one wants it as is.
Yum! Just made this and served it over a Caesar salad. Definitely a keeper. Easy, no muss no fuss. With always on hand ingredients!

Easiest Blackened Chicken Haiku: "Sure, it is easy, but blackened is a dry rub, cooked fast on high heat." I didn't change a thing about this simple recipe, but I don't really see how it's blackened (well, other than the actual color of the chicken when finished) as I thought that a blackened protein was when it's coated in a dry rub and browned super fast on really high heat. Hey either way, this was easy to do, but I thought that the Worcestershire flavor was just too, too much.
The initial taste was great, then the spiciness hit. I didn't realize it would be spicy and I can't serve it to my 2 year old.
We could not eat this. It was like eating straight pepper. Would not make again.
Excellant dish exceptionally easy to make. Chicken was very moist and well seasoned. The only change I made was to add a sprinkling of cayenne pepper. I will definately make this again.
Fixed this tonight for my hubby and me, served with brown rice.... A winner it was...ty
I was surprised at how good this turned out. I added a dash of Tony's Cajun Seasoning to the sauce--whoowhee! That's good eatin' dere!
Easy, simple, tasty...perfect for a quick meal. I complemented the chicken with wild rice for a nice mix. Adding it to alfredo and pasta sounds great too.
